title: Natural projection to the two-term naive cotangent truncation
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $P\twoheadrightarrow B$ a surjective $A$-algebra map, where $P$ is a polynomial $A$-algebra on any set of variables or a localization of such an algebra. Put $J=\ker(P\to B)$ and $C(P)=[J/J^2\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\Omega^1_{P/A}\otimes_P B]$ in degrees $-1,0$, where $\mathrm d([h])=\mathrm dh\otimes1$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. For the standard cotangent complex [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] in $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], there is a canonical map $L_{B/A}\to C(P)$ inducing an isomorphism $\tau_{\geq-1}L_{B/A}\simeq C(P)$. Truncation means replacing degree $-1$ by the cokernel of the incoming differential and discarding degrees below $-1$. This comparison is natural under commutative diagrams of such surjective presentations: a compatible map $P\to P'$ over $A\to A'$ and $B\to B'$ gives the semilinear chain map $C(P)\to C(P')$, with $[h]\mapsto[h']$ in degree $-1$ and $\mathrm dp\otimes b\mapsto\mathrm dp'\otimes b'$ in degree $0$, and it commutes in the derived category with the standard functoriality map on $L$. No vanishing below degree $-1$ and no finite generation of the differential module is asserted.

proof.text: Put $R=A[B]$, $I=\ker(R\to B)$ and let $K$ be the standard differential complex of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. By [lem-trf-standard-cotangent-chain-projection] its face-difference map $c:K\to C(R)$ is a chain map with degree-zero identity and strictly commutes with standard ring-square maps. Apply [lem-trf-standard-cotangent-boundary-cokernel] to its degree-minus-one map $\rho$: the hypothesis $\rho\partial_2=0$ is supplied by the first node. It identifies the good-truncation term $M_1/\operatorname{im}\partial_2$ with $I/I^2$, intertwining the remaining differential since $\delta\rho=\partial_1$. Hence the induced map $\tau_{\geq-1}K\to C(R)$ is an isomorphism of complexes and gives the asserted standard-presentation isomorphism in $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tags 08UP (remark-explicit-comparison-map) and 08RB (lemma-relation-with-naive-cotangent-complex): explicit cokernel calculation completing the omitted low-degree comparison verification.

proof.text: For the given $P\twoheadrightarrow B$, choose a lift $a:R\to P$ over $B$. Its existence and the homotopy equivalence $C(a):C(R)\to C(P)$ follow from [lem-trf-localized-presentation-homotopy-equivalence], applied to the polynomial presentation $R=A[B]$. The induced maps and their generator formulas are those of [lem-trf-conormal-semilinear-difference-homotopy]. Define the comparison as $Q(C(a))Q(c)$ in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Two choices of $a$ are homotopic by the difference-homotopy node, so this derived morphism is independent of the choice. Writing $\bar c:\tau_{\geq-1}K\to C(R)$ for Step 1's induced chain isomorphism, the factor through the truncation is $Q(C(a))Q(\bar c)$. It factors the original comparison since $c=\bar c\pi$, where $\pi:K\to\tau_{\geq-1}K$ is the good-truncation projection. Both factors are invertible: $\bar c$ is a chain isomorphism and $C(a)$ is a homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy), proof of part (4), with Tag 04EG (lemma-localization-formally-etale) for the square-zero lift: extension of the polynomial-presentation argument to localized polynomial presentations.

proof.text: For a presentation map $p:P\to P\prime$ over a ring square, choose lifts $a:R\to P$ and $a\prime:R\prime=A\prime[B\prime]\to P\prime$. Write $s:R\to R\prime$ for the standard variable map. The maps $pa$ and $a\prime s$ have the same reduction to $B\prime$, so [lem-trf-conormal-semilinear-difference-homotopy] gives $C(p)C(a)\simeq C(a\prime)C(s)$. By strict naturality of $c$ in [lem-trf-standard-cotangent-chain-projection], this homotopy gives the required commuting derived square [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with target scalars restricted along $B\to B\prime$. Explicitly, $Q(C(p))Q(C(a))Q(c)=Q(C(a\prime))Q(c\prime)Q(K(s))$, using $C(s)c=c\prime K(s)$. The standard map represents cotangent functoriality by [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. The formulas for $C(p)$ are exactly those in the difference-homotopy node. Only the good truncation was used; there is no assertion of lower vanishing or finite generation.
